payload.task_text:
I am a department chair preparing a self-study report for our upcoming program accreditation review. There is a PDF document in the workspace called accreditation_standards.pdf that outlines eight accreditation criteria our program must meet, each with a specific minimum threshold. Please start by reading this PDF to understand all the criteria and their requirements.

Next, pull course data from our learning management system. Get the full list of courses offered in our program, and for each course retrieve the enrollment count, average submission grade, and average quiz score. Focus especially on the two Creative Computing and Culture course sections (courses 7 and 8) since those are our flagship offerings and the accreditation reviewers always look at them closely.

There is also a file called previous_review.csv in the workspace with results from our last accreditation cycle, and a file called faculty_credentials.json listing our faculty qualifications. Use these as reference when assessing compliance.

Write and run a Python script called compute_metrics.py in the workspace that reads the course data you gathered and computes program-level metrics. The script should calculate the overall average GPA across all courses by averaging the per-course average grades on a 0-100 scale (i.e. the mean of the per-course average submission grades) and store it under the key avg_gpa, the retention proxy which is total enrollment divided by total submission count across all courses, and an assessment diversity score computed as the number of courses that have both assignments and quizzes divided by the total number of courses. The script should output its results to program_metrics.json in the workspace.

Then write and run a second script called evaluate_compliance.py that reads the accreditation criteria from accreditation_standards.pdf (you can hardcode the thresholds you extracted earlier) and the program_metrics.json file, and evaluates each of the eight criteria. For each criterion it should determine a status of Compliant if the metric meets or exceeds the threshold, Partial if within 10 percent of the threshold, or Non-Compliant if below. Output the results to compliance_assessment.json.

Create an Excel workbook in the workspace called Accreditation_Self_Study.xlsx with four sheets. The first sheet Course_Data should have columns Course_Name, Enrollment, Avg_Grade, Quiz_Avg, and Assignment_Count, with one row per course sorted alphabetically. The second sheet Accreditation_Matrix should have columns Criterion, Threshold, Actual_Value, and Status with one row per accreditation criterion. The third sheet Gap_Analysis should have columns Criterion, Gap_Description, Remediation_Action, and Timeline, with rows only for criteria that are Partial or Non-Compliant. The fourth sheet Resource_Needs should have columns Resource, Justification, Estimated_Cost, and Priority, listing at least three resources needed to address compliance gaps such as additional faculty hires, assessment software, or curriculum redesign consulting. Write all numeric cells as literal numbers (do not write Excel formulas); a threshold or value may be written as a plain number (e.g. 78, 0.65) or as a string with a percent sign (e.g. '78.0%') — both are acceptable.

Create a database in the team knowledge base called "Accreditation Action Items" with properties Criterion as title, Status as a select field with options Compliant and Partial and Non-Compliant, Owner as rich text, Due_Date as date, and Evidence as rich text. Add one entry for each of the eight accreditation criteria. Set the status based on the compliance assessment results, assign owners from the faculty listed in faculty_credentials.json, set due dates spread across the next three months, and note what evidence is needed for each.

Check the shared calendar for any existing accreditation-related events. Then create three new calendar events. First an event called "Evidence Collection Deadline" scheduled for 30 days from now. Second an event called "Draft Report Due" scheduled for 60 days from now. Third an event called "Final Submission" scheduled for 90 days from now. Each event should include a description mentioning the accreditation self-study.

Finally, write and run a script called generate_summary.py that reads the compliance assessment results and produces a plain text file called accreditation_summary.txt in the workspace. This summary should list each criterion with its status, highlight any gaps found, and state the overall compliance percentage explicitly (for example: "Overall compliance: 75%").

Work in the shared workspace and shared databases. Complete the steps in order and create each artifact (script, json, workbook, database, page, calendar event) exactly once — do not duplicate the Notion database, its eight pages, or the calendar events, and do not overwrite a completed file with a partial version.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, keep Canvas collection on explore, keep the sequential processor scripts on one local writer, then parallelize the independent workbook, Notion, and calendar artifacts. A wave must finish and return all stated handoffs before the next wave begins.

Before Wave 1, the main agent reads `accreditation_standards.pdf`, `previous_review.csv`, and `faculty_credentials.json` in read-only mode, freezes the eight criteria and exact minimum thresholds, and calls `canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true)` once. Validate unique IDs/codes/full names and freeze the complete 22-course manifest. Partition that manifest into two disjoint shards covering every `course_id` exactly once: shard A = course_id 1-11 (AAA-2013J through DDD-2013B, including flagship courses 7 and 8) and shard B = course_id 12-22 (DDD-2014B through GGG-2014B). Pass each owner its literal ID list, codes, and full names.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 explore sub-agents in parallel:

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Course-metrics owner for shard A (course_id 1-11, including Creative Computing and Culture courses 7 and 8). For each assigned course, verify the course, enumerate its assignments and quizzes, and gather enrollment, per-course average submission grade, average quiz score (accepted only once quiz-to-assignment mappings and complete student score coverage are proven), assignment/submission counts, and a both-assessments flag. Persist `accreditation_course_batch_a.json` with `coverage_status=complete` plus provenance controls, or `=blocked` with the exact gap and unsupported quiz averages omitted. Return only path/hash and coverage controls. Make no other writes.
   2. explore 1 (enterprise-data-analyst 1): Course-metrics owner for shard B (course_id 12-22) — same literal recipe, only that shard's course identities and `accreditation_course_batch_b.json` substituted.

After Wave 1, the main agent requires both shards together to cover every frozen `course_id` exactly once, rejects duplicate/missing IDs, and requires courses 7 and 8 to be present. Freeze both batch paths/hashes plus the eight PDF thresholds.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 1 coder sub-agent:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Sole owner of the processor chain. It receives both frozen course batches and the eight frozen thresholds. First merge both batches into one unified dataset covering every course, verifying no duplicates and that courses 7 and 8 are included, with any missing course recorded in a warnings list. Write and run a Python-standard-library-only `compute_metrics.py` that writes `program_metrics.json` with literal numeric values: `avg_gpa` as the mean of the per-course `avg_grade` values (non-null only, 0-100 scale), `retention_proxy` as total_enrollment divided by total_submissions, and `diversity_score` as the number of courses with both assignments and quizzes (a non-null `avg_quiz_score` counts as evidence of quizzes when `quiz_count` is missing) divided by the total number of courses — each rounded to 4 decimal places — plus `total_courses`, `total_enrollment`, `total_submissions`, `courses_with_assignments_and_quizzes`, and a warnings list. If `total_submissions` is 0 set `retention_proxy` to null with a warning; if some courses lack `total_submissions`, compute `retention_proxy` from the courses that have it and list the excluded courses in warnings. Then write and run `evaluate_compliance.py` with the eight criteria and thresholds hardcoded, mapping `avg_gpa` to the overall-GPA criterion, the retention proxy to the retention criterion, and the assessment diversity score to the assessment-diversity criterion, writing `compliance_assessment.json` containing a `criteria` array of exactly eight objects with fields `criterion`, `threshold`, `actual_value`, `status`, and optionally `gap_note`. Status rules: Compliant when `actual_value >= threshold`, Partial when `actual_value >= 0.9 x threshold` (within 10 percent below), Non-Compliant otherwise; a criterion with no matching metric gets `actual_value` null, status Non-Compliant, and a `gap_note` explaining the missing metric. Then write and run `generate_summary.py` that reads `compliance_assessment.json` and produces `accreditation_summary.txt` listing every one of the eight criteria with its exact name and status one per line, a Gaps section for each Partial or Non-Compliant criterion showing its actual value vs threshold and a short statement of the shortfall, and a final line of exactly `Overall compliance: <NN>%` where NN is (Compliant count / 8) * 100 rounded to the nearest whole number. If `compliance_assessment.json` is missing or unreadable, write `accreditation_summary.txt` stating that compliance data was unavailable and giving the line `Overall compliance: N/A`. Run the three scripts in that order only. Return paths/hashes and metric/status/summary controls. Do not create the workbook, Notion database, or calendar events.

After Wave 2, the main agent verifies and freezes `program_metrics.json`, `compliance_assessment.json`, and `accreditation_summary.txt` as the sole downstream source.

3. Wave 3 — dispatch exactly 3 coder sub-agents in parallel:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 1): Sole writer of `Accreditation_Self_Study.xlsx`. Read only the frozen course packet and compliance result. Create exactly four worksheets in order — `Course_Data` (one row per course sorted alphabetically by name, including courses 7 and 8), `Accreditation_Matrix` (exactly eight criterion rows with threshold, actual value, and status), `Gap_Analysis` (rows only for Partial or Non-Compliant criteria, with gap description, remediation action, and timeline), and `Resource_Needs` (at least three resources each justified against a specific gap, with literal-number estimated cost and High/Medium/Low priority). All cells must be literal values, never Excel formulas. Read every populated range back.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Sole Notion owner of the database `Accreditation Action Items`. Search the exact title first, create it once only when absent, and reuse without duplicating. Require properties Criterion (title), Status (select: Compliant/Partial/Non-Compliant), Owner, Due_Date, and Evidence. Add exactly eight pages: one per criterion named and statused per the frozen compliance result, each with a distinct faculty owner from `faculty_credentials.json`, due dates spread across the next three months (none in the past), and an evidence note referencing the program metrics and source data. Read the database and page properties back.
   3. coder 2 (external-workflow-operator 1): Sole calendar owner of the three accreditation milestones. Search existing accreditation-related events first, then create without duplicating `Evidence Collection Deadline` (exactly 30 days after today), `Draft Report Due` (60 days), and `Final Submission` (90 days), each with a description mentioning the accreditation self-study and no backdated times. Read the retained events back.

After Wave 3, the main agent reconciles the workbook, Notion eight-page set, three calendar events, and summary text against the same frozen compliance result. Do not dispatch more sub-agents.

You are collecting read-only LMS (Canvas) statistics for a department accreditation self-study. You must NOT write any files; you only report data in your final message.

Courses to collect: course IDs [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]

For EACH course_id in your group, do in order:
1) Call canvas_list_assignments(course_id). Record every assignment's id and points_possible. Count assignments.
2) Call canvas_list_quizzes(course_id). Record every quiz's id, title, and its assignment_id link. Count quizzes.
3) For EACH assignment id from step 1, call canvas_list_assignment_submissions(course_id=<cid>, assignment_id=<aid>, page=1, per_page=1). The response includes a "summary" object that covers the WHOLE assignment server-side; record summary.total_count and summary.avg_score from it. Do NOT fetch additional submission pages, do NOT call canvas_list_student_submissions, and do NOT fetch quiz submissions - the summary object is all that is needed.

Rules:
- Read-only: no writes, uploads, or creations of any kind.
- Do not paste raw endpoint dumps into your report.
- If summary.avg_score is null, record null (and treat count as 0).

Final deliverable: emit exactly ONE JSON code block in your final message with this exact structure (one key per course id, as a string):
{
  "<course_id>": {
    "assignment_count": <int>,
    "quiz_count": <int>,
    "assignments": [{"assignment_id": <int>, "points_possible": "<str>", "total_count": <int>, "avg_score": <float or null>}, ...],
    "quizzes": [{"quiz_id": <int>, "assignment_id": <int>, "title": "<str>"}]
  }
}
Also state in one sentence that every course in your group completed successfully (or name any course/call that failed).
Collect Canvas assignment/quiz stats per course

Task: create Notion artifacts in the team knowledge base (Notion workspace) for an accreditation self-study. Create each item EXACTLY ONCE (check with API-post-search first to avoid duplicates; a search for "Accreditation" should return nothing initially).

KNOWN ISSUE to work around: When calling mcp__notion__API-post-page, the `parent` parameter fails JSON-schema validation with "/parent must be object" for every encoding I tried in the main agent, including {"workspace": true, "type": "workspace"}, {"database_id": "<uuid>", "type": "database_id"}, and {"workspace": true}. The `properties` parameter (also an object) passed fine. Try these variations until one works:
1. parent as {"type": "workspace", "workspace": true}
2. parent as {"workspace": true} (no type)
3. parent as a database entry under the existing "Project Milestones" database (id de337798-fec4-4e3a-80ee-13717bc9b900): {"type": "database_id", "database_id": "de337798-fec4-4e3a-80ee-13717bc9b900"} with properties including the DB's Name title property and Status select ("Open") plus a title property.
4. If the mcp__notion__API-create-a-database inline parent schema behaves differently, you may create the database directly with parent {"type":"workspace","workspace":true} (its parent is declared permissive) — then no separate hub page is needed.
5. If object params seem stringified, also try passing the JSON escaped as a string.
Also note: if a workspace-parent page is not possible, a page created under the Project Milestones database is acceptable as the hub page.

STEP 1 — Hub page (skip only if step 4 succeeded): Create a page titled "Accreditation Self-Study" with this paragraph content:
"Team knowledge base page for the program accreditation self-study. Contains the Accreditation Action Items database tracking all eight accreditation criteria (C1-C8), owners, due dates, and evidence requirements. Compliance snapshot: 4 Compliant, 3 Partial, 1 Non-Compliant."
Record the new page's id.

STEP 2 — Database: Create a database titled "Accreditation Action Items" (parent = the hub page if you made one, else workspace). Properties (exact names):
- Criterion: title
- Status: select with options exactly "Compliant", "Partial", "Non-Compliant"
- Owner: rich_text
- Due_Date: date
- Evidence: rich_text
Record the database id.

STEP 3 — Add exactly 8 entries (one per criterion) via API-post-page with parent = database id. Use these rows (Criterion | Status | Owner | Due_Date | Evidence):
C1: Student Learning Outcomes | Partial | Dr. Sarah Chen | 2026-09-17 | LMS grade exports showing per-course average submission grades plus rubric calibration evidence for remediation.
C2: Assessment Diversity | Partial | Dr. Maria Santos | 2026-09-24 | Assessment inventory per course showing which sections combine assignments and quizzes, plus quiz additions to at least two sections.
C3: Student Retention | Non-Compliant | Dr. Elena Volkov | 2026-10-01 | Enrollment and submission-engagement reports, early-alert advising logs, and remediation plan for the retention proxy gap.
C4: Faculty Qualifications | Compliant | Dr. Michael Torres | 2026-10-31 | Faculty credentials file (faculty_credentials.json) verifying 8 of 10 faculty hold terminal degrees.
C5: Curriculum Coverage | Compliant | Dr. Lisa Nakamura | 2026-11-07 | Course catalog mapping 22 sections to 7 distinct subject areas.
C6: Course Enrollment Adequacy | Compliant | Dr. Thomas Anderson | 2026-11-14 | Registrar enrollment report showing average enrollment of 1481.5 students per section.
C7: Quiz-Based Assessment | Partial | Dr. Robert Kim | 2026-11-21 | Quiz score analysis per course (including flagship Creative Computing & Culture sections) and quiz remediation plan.
C8: Program Breadth | Compliant | Dr. Aisha Patel | 2026-11-28 | Schedule of all 22 course sections across all subjects.
Due_Date values are dates (e.g., {"start": "2026-09-17"}). Status must exactly match the select option names.

DELIVERABLE (final message): report success/failure for each step, plus the page id, database id, and the 8 created entry/page ids. Do not create anything beyond the items listed. Do not touch other Notion content.
Create Notion page + DB + 8 entries
